items.stem: Which statements about partial and total derivatives are true?
items.explanation: A, B and D are true; partials freeze one input, total derivatives include all changing inputs, and the gradient gives steepest ascent.
statements: In fₓ, y is held fixed
The total derivative includes all changing inputs
A directional derivative may use any non-unit vector without scaling
The gradient points in the direction of steepest increase

A.why: This is the definition of fₓ.

B.why: The chain rule includes every changing input.

D.why: The gradient direction maximises the directional derivative.

items.stem: The gradient is perpendicular to:
items.explanation: Along a level curve the function does not change to first order, so the gradient is normal.

items.stem: For f=x²y, fₓₓ is:

items.check: Differentiate with the stated variable held fixed, or apply the chain rule and verify by substitution.

items.stem: Which conditions support equality of mixed partials?
options: Continuity of the second partials near the point
items.explanation: Continuity of the relevant second partials is the standard sufficient condition.
statements: The relevant second partials are continuous in a neighbourhood
Only the first partials exist at the point

A.why: Clairaut's theorem applies under continuity of second partials.
